questions.q: In a script, a phone rings; the heroine crosses the room, sets down a cup and turns on a lamp; then she decides not to answer. Which actions are the nuclei?
choices: The phone ringing and her decision not to answer
Crossing the room and setting down the cup
questions.explain: Nuclei are hinges where the story could go different ways; the rest are catalyzers.

questions.q: Which code raises enigmas, delays their answers and finally discloses the truth?
questions.explain: The hermeneutic code is the theory behind 'a question held open'.

questions.q: A reader sees a character pack a bag at night and instantly expects a departure. Which code is at work?
questions.explain: The proairetic code is sequences of actions we recognize from the first step because we've read them before.

questions.q: A mystery answers each question in the same scene it's asked, and audiences lose interest. What's missing?
choices: Delays: snares, partial answers and postponements in the hermeneutic code
questions.explain: Barthes shows that narrative works hard to delay its answers; the middle is delay.

questions.q: Where do the craft terms 'kernels and satellites' come from?
choices: Seymour Chatman, adapting Barthes's nuclei and catalyzers
questions.explain: Chatman's Story and Discourse (1978) renamed Barthes's 1966 distinction.

choices: A text with an obvious authorial voice
A text written for other writers
A text that makes the reader a producer of meaning, with no single way through
questions.explain: The readerly text offers a finished meaning; the writerly one asks the reader to make it.

questions.q: What is the main claim of 'The Death of the Author'?
choices: A text's meaning isn't fixed by its author's life and intentions but made in its reader
Authorship ended with the printing press
Only living authors can be interpreted
questions.explain: The essay ends by tying the birth of the reader to the death of the Author.

ideas: Every stretch of a story is woven from five codes, only two of which drive the reader forward in time.
Narrative raises a question and then labors to delay its answer with snares, equivocations and partial answers.
Some actions are hinges where a story could branch; others merely fill the space between hinges.
The birth of the reader must be at the cost of the death of the author.
